## 7 November report fragments and a separate telegram acknowledgment

<a id="november-7-report-fragments-and-a-separate-telegram-acknowledgment"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p151 A1, p151 A2, p151 B.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-fragment-and-acknowledgment-november-7-report-fragments-and-a-separate-telegram-acknowledgment"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p151 A, PDF page 154, is headed
`LP v NKJ (6.42 p.m., November 7th)` and `KR 1215 UKS 5 TLE`.
Only source-labeled parts **1 and 2** are established here. Parts 3–5
are not supplied or assembled from nearby messages. B is a separate
acknowledgment, with no established reply relationship to A.
All use the unchanged published partial **Nov7–9** key.

<a id="source-p151-a1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-fragment-and-acknowledgment-p151-a1"></a>

### p151 A1

The [source crop](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_A.png)
has **189 typed coordinates** against `1 TL RICHI-190`. The
[short-group detail](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_A1_short_group.png)
shows **AVVG**, four symbols. The following layers assume one missing
coordinate before that group: **?AVVG**. This is a conditional frame,
not a source-supplied loss position.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 190-coordinate frame with one missing coordinate at the AVVG short group:**

```text
OHLXBPXXNACHRICHTVONABREISEDEUTSCHERWAFFENSTILLSTANDSKOMMISSIONHATANSCHEINENDGEM?LDETENSTUR3FSS
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; one missing-coordinate fill and zero observed substitutions:**

```text
OHLXBPXXNACHRICHTVONABREISEDEUTSCHERWAFFENSTILLSTANDSKOMMISSIONHATANSCHEINENDGEMELDETENSTUR3FSS
```

</details>

The modeled missing coordinate at working index **55** is filled with D,
supplying E at plaintext position **80**. Its raw domain is **DEQTUX**.
The candidate fixes **95 / 95 positions** but retains the opaque ending
**STUR3FSS**; a fixed label is not necessarily an understood word.

**Readable German — spacing of an incomplete fragment, with the opaque closing retained:**

> OHL. BP. Nachricht von Abreise deutscher Waffenstillstandskommission
> hat anscheinend gemeldeten STUR3FSS

The predicate and closing are not reconstructed into a complete report.
The edition does not infer what effect the news of the commission's
departure had.

All five placements inside AVVG and all six coordinate values are
retained: **30 geometry-labeled witnesses**, **26 distinct complete
ciphertexts and plaintexts**. Requiring the lexical crib
**GEMELDETEN** at positions **77:87** leaves one candidate, the one above.
That uniqueness is conditional on both the one-loss model and the crib;
it is not an unconditional historical solution.

The later [p151/p157 copy comparison](157.md#edition-cases-military-armistice-departure-copy) supports
a separately priced A1 variant. Under the common-copy alignment, an
observed p157 coordinate supports p151 source index 142 `A` → `F`, giving
`STURZFSS` in place of `STUR3FSS`. The fuller `STURZDES` interpretation
still needs two additional p151 coordinate changes without observed p157
support. The truncated p157 source fixes **0/95 positions by itself** in
the declared frame; its copied prefix, competing alignments and conflicting
source choices remain explicit in the separate edition. The original
layers above retain their stated zero-observed-substitution candidate.

### p151 B

The [separate source](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_B.png)
is headed `NKJ v UKS (11.30 p.m., November 7th)` and `AN LP 2150`.
Its **156 typed coordinates** match `RICHI-156`. Five additional
[handwritten glyphs](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_B_annotation.png)
read **VXXDV**, duplicating the immediately preceding typed group.
The combined visible layer has **161 slots** and is odd in length.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — 156-coordinate typed source layer, with the five handwritten glyphs retained separately:**

```text
OXOXLXOPXDHRTIGESTELEGRAMMROEMX1ANOX11212OPXGEHXERHFLTENHOXKXMXOPXROEMX1A11302
```

**Edited output — same typed source layer; three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
OXHXLXOPXDORTIGESTELEGRAMMROEMX1ANOX11212OPXGEHXERHALTENHOXKXMXOPXROEMX1A11302
```

</details>

The changes are composite-source **0 F→V**, **40 V→F** and **115 X→D**.
They repair the first `O O L`, `DHRTIGES` and `ERHFLTEN`. The additional
H between ERHALTEN and O K M remains literal. Both layers have
**78 / 78 fixed positions**, and the complete edited candidate re-encrypts
exactly within the typed frame.

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, with abbreviation labels retained:**

> O. H. L. Op. Dortiges Telegramm Röm. 1 A No. 11212 Op. Geh. erhalten.
> H. O. K. M. Op. Röm. 1 A 11302.

The acknowledgment refers to the literal number **11212**. This edition
does not establish which other surviving message, if any, it answers.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov7-fragment-and-acknowledgment-conditional-interpretation-and-source-layer-accounting"></a>

### Conditional interpretation and source-layer accounting

B's primary reading selects the typed source layer, mapping each working
coordinate to the complete visible composite. The handwriting's author
and purpose are not established. If all 161 visible glyphs are instead
treated as transmitted material, reaching the typed frame requires
**five slot deletions**, involving five known coordinates under the
primary D reading. That is a separate conditional transmission model,
not a free repair. A hypothetical handwritten D→O sensitivity leaves
four known coordinates and one non-coordinate mask in those excluded
slots; it does not affect the typed output. The enlarged crop supports
D, so the O variant is not presented as equally certified.

The old B OCR omitted typed **XXVGF** and the final D, misread one typed
X and masked a handwritten D and typed V. Its exact reconstruction is
frozen in the [OCR snapshot](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/ocr_snapshot.json)
and [certificate](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/certificates.json).
The historical typed-layer choice is kept separate from those OCR fixes.

These three physical records have **536 visible glyph slots including
five handwritten annotations**, **531 typed coordinates**, and **532
modeled coordinates**, with **266 plaintext positions**. The raw layers
fix **265 / 266** and the edited layers **266 / 266** under their stated
frames/layers. The primary cost is **four observed substitutions and one
missing-coordinate fill**. Neither unresolved key symbol 5 nor 6 is
assigned: all used pairs are already resolved by the published baseline.

Earlier A1/A2 body candidates, B's unread OCR and key provenance are
preserved; no historical first-solution claim is made. See the
[inputs](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/inputs.json),
[reproduction instructions](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/README.md)
and the separate [Soldiers Council notice](#edition-cases-military-soldiers-council-surrender).

The [source crop](../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_C.png)

The unchanged published partial **Nov7–9** key gives a complete reading;

<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

```text
GOUVERNEMENTUNDUMRADIOLIEGENDEKASERNENHABENSICHSOLDATENRATERGEBENXRADIOXROUXX
```

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> Gouvernement und um Radio liegende Kasernen haben sich Soldatenrat

The record fixes **77 / 77 plaintext positions**, with zero coordinate

## p151 D2 — Notify the courier destination and report arrival

**Edition context:** Munich couriers carrying radio operating documents.

**Related source pages:** [p153 D2](153.md#source-p153-d2), [p153 E1](153.md#source-p153-e1), [p158 C2](158.md#source-p158-c2), [p162 A1](162.md#source-p162-a1).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-munich-couriers-carrying-radio-operating-documents"></a>


[Source and certificate](../experiments/courier_recovery/README.md)

Five records intercepted on 9 November concern couriers carrying radio operating documents to Munich: first parts p153 E1 / p162 A1 and continuations p151 D2 / p153 D2 / p158 C2. The best continuation fixes **67 of 68 positions** under the published Nov7–9 key; the damaged first part has a conditional 134-position reconstruction. The unit numeral remains **{5,6}** in the key, with a historical argument for **6** below.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

The first part is an editorial reconstruction with the source costs below:

**Readable German:**

> An Ingenieurinspektion Muenchen. Gefr. Geraus und Feldgr. Mahrer als
> Kurier mit Funkbetriebsunterlagen fuer Grukonach{5,6}02 7 Uhr abds.
> nach dort abgefahren.

The best-preserved second-part witness, p158 C2, reads directly without any
source-coordinate change:

**Readable German:**

> Grukonach{5,6}02 benachrichtigen. Eintreffen hierher drahten.
> Nachrchef 4 B 49909.

**Meaning:** The proposed first part tells the Engineer Inspectorate in
Munich that the two named men left at 7 p.m. as couriers carrying radio
operating documents for `GRUKONACH?02`. The continuation instructs the
recipient to notify that unit and telegraph the arrival back to the sender.

The names `GERAUS` and `MAHRER` remain unidentified; their U and H are not supported across every fit of both alignment models. The reading retains the unexpanded `FELDGR` and singular `ALS KURIER`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-what-is-directly-supported"></a>

### Direct evidence from the second-part copies

All three second-part records contain exactly 136 coordinates. Under the
known partial square, each fixes 67 of 68 plaintext positions. The p158 C2
text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GRUKONACH?02BENACHRICHTIGENEINTREFFENHIERHERDRAHTENXNACHRCHEF4B49909
```

</details>

The p151 D2 repeat has `GRU1ONACH` at the beginning, and p153 D2 has
`BENACHWICHTIGEN`; the source edition preserves both. The unaltered p158
witness independently supplies the readable forms of both words.

The question mark denotes the observed pair **VF**, whose unassigned square value is **5 or 6**.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-a-separately-linked-conditional-reading-grukonach602"></a>

#### A separately linked conditional reading: GRUKONACH602

The [9 November operational reports](166.md#edition-cases-military-nov9-operational-reports-historical-identification-most-likely-the-6th-reserve-division) use the same **VF** cell for a reserve-division numeral. A contemporary French telegram identifies the matching formation as the **6th Reserve Division**. Under that historical identification, **VF=6**, and both courier fields read **GRUKONACH602** with no additional source-coordinate changes.

This is one historical inference applied through a shared key cell. The base domain remains 5/6; the first-part reconstruction and its association with the continuation retain the assumptions below. The [context certificate](../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json) records the external source, its date limits and the earlier p176b application.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-first-part-damage-and-explicit-reconstruction-cost"></a>

### First-part damage and explicit reconstruction cost

The first parts both advertise 268 coordinates but actually preserve 259
and 264 slots. Both visibly contain the six-letter group `VXDVDD`, which
the transcription retains. One overstruck glyph in p162 A1 is masked as a
source erasure; its displayed reading is kept separately.

Comparing the two sources without the key finds a five-slot relative gap:
all 260 possible gap starts were tested, and seven tied starts, 151–157,
leave only two known-coordinate disagreements. This does not locate the
other four slots missing from the longer witness.

For the **stated 134-position candidate**, exact alignment gives:

| Alignment model | p153 E1 | p162 A1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retain every source coordinate | Insert 9 slots; change 6 known coordinates; 32 tied minimum fits | Insert 4 slots; change 8 known coordinates; 2 tied minimum fits |
| Delete one received coordinate | Delete 1, insert 10; change 4 known coordinates; 192 tied minimum fits | Delete 1, insert 5; change 6 known coordinates; 14 tied minimum fits |

Every deletion position and tied optimum is retained. A fill of the overstruck p162 glyph is charged separately from observed-coordinate changes.

Within the first model, **123/134 proposed positions** have an unchanged coordinate pair in at least one witness for every combination of minimum fits. Requiring that support under both models gives **118/134**. These counts are conditional on the proposed wording and alignment families. The [certificate](../experiments/courier_recovery/certificate.json) includes all raw masked-frame readings and exact costs.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-association-source-and-credit"></a>

### Association, source and credit

The two first-part records explicitly say first part of two, and all three
continuations say second part. The p153 D/E headers both read `RVV v N4` on
the same morning; the first-part `2120 (SY)` field also fits the p151 D
`SY v N4` continuation. Both bodies use the same unresolved `GRUKONACH?02`
field, and the instruction to report arrival follows naturally from the
departure notice. These facts support the association, but the typed log
does not explicitly cross-reference the parts as one original transmission.
The direct continuation remains readable independently of that association.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp151, 153, 158 and 162 / PDF page 154, 156, 161 and 165,
in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source inputs](../experiments/courier_recovery/inputs.json) give
literal rows, headers and reproducible image rectangles. The Nov7–9 key
retains its historical and George Lasry / coauthor attribution in
[the key register](../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, repeated-copy recovery, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

```sh
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/build.py --verify
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/verify.py
```

## p151 E2 — Operations-map sheets for the Gleiwitz garrison

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-operations-map-sheets-operations-map-sheets-for-the-gleiwitz-garrison"></a>



**Source restoration and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-operations-map-sheets-p151-e2"></a>

### p151 E2

This surviving second part lists operations-map sheets at the directly
read scale **1 zu 100000**, with named sheet areas and quantities, followed
by a Gleiwitz garrison-office address. The complete printed body has
**224 slots** and decrypts under the unchanged published **Nov7–9** key.
Two explicitly priced word substitutions and two printed-erasure fills
produce 110 fixed labels out of 112. The conservative layer retains the final two labels as globally
coupled unknown digits; the optional reference reading is given above.

The [Childs source, printed p151, section E](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view)
prints `LP v NKJ`, `7.09 a.m., November 9th`, `2 TL` and `RICHI-224`.
Its full page and enlarged E crop were directly inspected. The source PDF,
page, crop rectangle, dimensions and decoded-pixel digest are pinned in
[the inputs](../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/inputs.json).
The [verifier](../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/verify.py)
recreates those pixels when given the PDF; the source is not represented
by an unavailable image link.

The manuscript has 44 five-slot groups and the four-character final group
`XDVV`. Group 16 is **GGVVX**. Earlier repository OCR gave **GGVVXX**, an
extra unprinted `X`, which changed the length to 225. Restoring the actual
five-coordinate group repairs the digital transcription; it excludes no
coordinate from the manuscript. The OCR snapshot and its odd-length
arithmetic remain in the experiment for comparison.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-operations-map-sheets-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies the closing **AOK 11, 1d 7065**, completing the two remaining labels at no additional source edit or fill. The opposite square gives 7056. The map scale, sheet names and quantities are already read independently of this choice.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-operations-map-sheets-raw-and-optional-edited-readings"></a>

### Raw and optional edited readings

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — all 224 printed source slots in order, with the two dashes and unknown key cells retained:**

```text
OPERATIONSKA0TE1ZU100000SALZ?URGWIENLE?BERGBRESLAUJE40BLATTXWARSCHAU10BLATTANGARNISONKDOGLEIWVTZFSXAOK11X1D70??X
```

**Edited output — two observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or changed key:**

```text
OPERATIONSKARTE1ZU100000SALZBURGWIENLEMBERGBRESLAUJE40BLATTXWARSCHAU10BLATTANGARNISONKDOGLEIWITZFSXAOK11X1D70??X
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete optional stream, retaining the literal separators, quantities and closing labels:**

> Operationskarte 1 zu 100000 Salzburg Wien Lemberg Breslau je 40 Blatt X Warschau 10 Blatt an Garnisonkdo Gleiwitz FS X AOK 11 X 1D70?? X.

**Conditional interpretation:** The fragment lists operations maps at
1:100,000, forty sheets each for the areas labeled Salzburg, Wien, Lemberg
and Breslau, and ten sheets for Warschau. It gives the garrison command at
Gleiwitz as the delivery address. The `FS`, `AOK11` and `1D70??` fields are
retained without reconstructing their administrative meaning. The absent
first part and any evidence of actual dispatch or receipt are not supplied.

The named-place spellings in this reading are source-language labels. Two
of their letters are fills and one is a substitution, as shown below;
identifying a familiar name does not make the supplied letter an observation.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-operations-map-sheets-exact-word-costs"></a>

### Exact word costs

All indices are zero-based. Every received coordinate stays in its original
slot; the two dashes in printed group `XGG--` are source slots 103 and 104.

| Plaintext position | Raw → proposed label | Raw pair → edited pair | Source operation | Word |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | `0` → `R` | `VD` → `AD` | Source 1, `V` → `A` | `KA0TE` → `KARTE` |
| 28 | `?` → `B` | `G?` → `GX` | Fill printed dash 103 with `X` | `SALZ?URG` → `SALZBURG` |
| 38 | `?` → `M` | `A?` → `AF` | Fill printed dash 104 with `F` | `LE?BERG` → `LEMBERG` |
| 93 | `V` → `I` | `GA` → `GG` | Source 53, `A` → `G` | `GLEIWVTZ` → `GLEIWITZ` |

Before the fills, the two name positions have domains **29BITV** and
**MPRUWY**, respectively. The proposed `B` and `M` belong to those domains,
but the surviving half-pairs do not uniquely select them. The scale
`1ZU100000`, quantities `40` and `10`, and `AOK11` are already raw labels;
none is introduced by the word repairs.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-operations-map-sheets-the-two-unresolved-digits-are-coupled"></a>

### The two unresolved digits are coupled

The remaining unknown positions use **different unassigned square cells**.
All source coordinates in these two pairs are observed.

| Plaintext position | Observed pair | Original source indices | Literal domain |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 109 | `VF` | 212, 43 | `5` or `6` |
| 110 | `XA` | 66, 134 | `5` or `6` |

A single injective square must govern both cells. The only complete
assignments and corresponding closing strings are:

| VF label | XA label | Literal closing field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 6 | `1D7056` |
| 6 | 5 | `1D7065` |

Both full-key witnesses re-encrypt the complete edited stream exactly.
They are mathematical alternatives, not historical numeral assignments;
`1D7055` and `1D7066` would violate the unchanged square's injectivity.
The main reading therefore retains **1D70??**.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-operations-map-sheets-evidence-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence and reproduction

The [certificate](../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/certificates.json)
contains all 112 raw and edited pair maps, the four changes, both unresolved
domains, both complete global-key witnesses and the retained earlier OCR
comparison. The experiment's [reproduction guide](../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/README.md)
gives the source metadata and optional original-PDF pixel check.

**Reviewed source crops:** [p151_reviewed.png](../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/sources/p151_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

```sh
python experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/verify.py --verify --pdf /tmp/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

The source is **J. Rives Childs**. The published period keys retain the
credit of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** (2016)
and George Lasry's 2017 key disclosure, as recorded in the unchanged key
metadata. This edition is a source restoration and explicit editorial
review by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**, with earlier repository OCR
preserved and no claim to universal first-decipherment priority.
